items.title: Slide Hampton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: you did stuff with Curtis Fuller

ctx.x: Anyway, Lloyd Price. Talk about some of the personnel that was there besides Marcus Belgrave.

We had – a lot of guys played with Lloyd. A lot of people don’t know. Like Jimmy Heath, Curtis Fuller, Marcus Belgrave. A couple of really great piano players played with him. Of course nobody ever got to know about that. But they were trying to upgrade their music. They wanted to get into the new century of music that was coming on. I wish I could have helped them more.
What caused you to depart from Motown?

items.title: Curtis Fuller — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: There’s no greater writer now than Slide Hampton, you know? ... I know once, I can really say, and he would acknowledge, it was the most overwritten piece of music I’ve ever heard.

ctx.x: They were in the process of de-segregating?

It was the last black army band, yeah. Slide Hampton’s brother, he was processed through there. They were, you know, I think the full script was 28. Everybody didn’t play a horn; they had many administrative people. Cannonball couldn’t be head of it because he wasn’t the warrant officer. They gave him a staff sergeant thing because they sent him up here to the Naval School of Music. He passed that course. He got to be the band director, but he wasn’t in charge. He couldn’t be because he was a staff sergeant. You…
